source_time_discretization: Each release quadrature point is assigned to the next grid boundary (delay<dt), and pellet-flight integrals use left-continuous intervals. This prevents any outgoing gas from a pulse leaking numerically into its own earlier incoming flight.

cases.interpretation: Pressure is the volume-averaged trace of the kinetic stress tensor, with a separate energy-weighted survival kernel; it is not a local wall/plume value. Gas molecules are ballistic and absorbed at their first return. Background at t0 represents a steady constant source before t0; then actual chronological emissions replace it. The radial column uses exact spherical chord geometry. Pellet exposure uses quasi-static radial columns averaged over each flight; thermal gas speeds are small compared with selected pellet speeds.

scope: Every case uses actual final350 stage outputs and focus times. Full release and f=1 are response normalizations, not measured desorption fractions. Multiply H and He responses separately by their own cavity injection fractions.
Capture g includes aperture area, molecular transmission and irreversible routing into the closed return/product line. A hot wall bounce is not removal.

Well-mixed balance is a conditional diffuse model, with finite initial steady reservoirs. It is not a local plume bound. The separate first-flight kernel tests transient spherical geometry at g1 only.
Gas collision cross sections, charged-plume fields, side-channel backstream, coating ablation and dust are separate screens.
All mass is retained somewhere in the station: a source delay, pumping, heating or ionization does not create permanent loss.
